decision: Use the existing canonical KWin focus observation for the existing Kitty native-input qualification when KDE is the configured backend.
reason: The existing GNOME-only probe cannot classify KDE terminals. The shared canonical KWin provider is authenticated, but the first candidate also rejected real Kitty windows: KWin desktopFileName is empty while resourceClass is exactly kitty. Captured Observe messages show this for ordinary and owned Kitty launches; no text authority is inferred from metadata. A changed-byte native trace then shows no probe despite Kitty caps 9 and cell width 9: the admitted engine has no legacy focus_receipt. Use the existing live AdmissionToken exact_field_receipt projection for this existing qualification, rather than a fallback identity.

consequences.owner: Existing KWin focus provider and the existing field-bound Kitty probe; share its source module, do not copy its implementation or introduce another text/output owner.
consequences.scope: KDE uses the existing canonical provider. Require canonical nonempty identity, exact kitty resource class, and an appId that is either empty (observed KWin desktopFileName), kitty, or kitty.desktop. Missing or conflicting app metadata, another class, and missing identity grant nothing. GNOME stable-window read and current IBus focus receipt binding remain unchanged. Classification alone never creates a deletion grant: KnownStart, token, observed-boundary, snapshot and verifier checks remain. No delivery-route changes, synthetic client acknowledgements or second ownership policy. On context-admission input, obtain and revalidate the qualification receipt only from the current live AdmissionToken. Legacy input retains its actual focus receipt. Never fall back to a legacy receipt in an admitted engine; loss of the token invalidates the cached classification. FocusOut still clears it. This projection is for the existing qualification only, not a client acknowledgement or a new text owner. Native receipt terminal-kwin-context-receipt-v1 proves a cursor callback reaches the probe only after the first typed letter entered owned preedit. Reuse that same bounded one-shot probe immediately before choosing the first printable word mode, when the current admitted token and previously observed cursor are available. Cursor callbacks retain the same helper; no second policy, timer, retry, client-specific output path or mode change for an already-owned composition is introduced. A manual gesture after a layout handoff may have no new printable key. Reuse the same helper after begin_context_bridge_output and before WindowInteraction::admit_manual_toggle, retaining its live field revalidation and once-per-focus cache. The existing bridge/token and target authority checks remain mandatory.
consequences.failure: Unavailable, busy or non-Kitty evidence grants nothing. Existing stale-focus rejection remains. Canonical provider read/cleanup budgets remain 250/25 ms; measure native latency.
consequences.rollback: Revert this decision-scoped qualification change; no installed user process or desktop service restarts required.
consequences.test_organization: Move the two daemon focus-consumer checks into focus_guard tests, retaining UUID, tab narrowing and failure assertions. Canonical provider security tests remain with the shared provider and execute in both binaries. The first attempt is a compile failure, not semantic RED.
